messages.author: d994cff5897faec8
messages.subject: Discrete X scale with legend
parts:
I have a data set with a series of 11 conditions that are ordered and
named. I'd like to show them as a numbered sequence along the X-axis
but have a legend mapping numbers to names (the names are quite long).
Is it possible to do that?

zw

messages.author: 223beb57ce203bde
messages.subject: Re: Discrete X scale with legend
parts:
Hi,

This is NOT a real solution, but it does what you want (see the
attached figure)...

############## START #########
df <- data.frame(
x = factor(paste('name', letters[c(1:5)]), ordered=T),
y = 5:1)

df$id <- as.numeric(df$x)
# or the following line, if you have more than 10 levels
# df$id <- letters[as.numeric(df$x)]

ggplot(df, aes(factor(id), y)) +
geom_point(aes(shape = x), size = 2.5) +
scale_shape_manual(values = as.character(df$id)) +
geom_point(size = 2.6)
############# END ###########

Xie Chao

messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Re: Discrete X scale with legend
parts:
> I have a data set with a series of 11 conditions that are ordered and
> named.  I'd like to show them as a numbered sequence along the X-axis
> but have a legend mapping numbers to names (the names are quite long).
>  Is it possible to do that?

Not a direct answer to your question but have you tried rotating the
x-axis labels (use the axis.text.x theme property)? Is it not enough
to accommodate the long names? If it's not, then it means your legend
will be huge anyway.

JiHO
